name: toy_write
description: Write a toy: a file set with main.lua required and asset files beside it (the studio's packed-toy shape, docs/STUDIO.md §2). Compiles main.lua with renderer/pce-il.js immediately and returns the IL's refusal code and file:line if it does not lower, and compiles the song files (song.json, songs.json) the way music(index) needs them. Replaces the current toy and clears any run.

files.description: the toy's files; main.lua is the one that runs

name: toy_save
description: Save the loaded toy as the studio's own file (#160): one pce.studio/1 JSON envelope holding main.lua, every asset file, the named sources (sources.json) and the songs, written by the same builder renderer/studio.html's Save uses (renderer/pce-source.js envelopeText) — there is no second format. The person opens it in the studio with Open… → From file, or drops it on the page, and plays the toy WITH its art. The path is relative to the folder the server was started in; a path outside it is refused (save-path).

path.description: the file to write, inside the working folder; .pce.json is added when the name has no .pce.json or .pce.studio extension

title.description: the toy's title, shown in the studio's tab (default: the file's own name)

name: toy_run
description: Run the loaded toy's main.lua for `frames` video frames (0..frames-1) through the IL runtime, with an optional pad script, and return the final state: registers, raster table shape, VRAM/CRAM/SAT digests, log lines, PSG write count and per-channel sound activity (notes started and the instrument each sounds with), so music() can be seen without hearing it. The toy's asset files are imported into VRAM/CRAM/SAT before init() (#117) and the song files are its music(index) slots (#161). A run is fresh and deterministic; t is f/60, not the clock.

pad.description: held-button intervals; pads are 1..5 and a button name is up, down, left, right, i, ii, select, run

name: source_add
description: Add art or a song to the toy (#153, #161): a picture — a base64 PNG, or a hand-drawn pixel grid with its palette — becomes tiles, sprites, a tilesheet or a palette through the Add Source importer (renderer/pce-source.js importImage, #123) and is merged into the toy's asset files: tiles.json replaced for a background picture, sprites.json appended (new palette rows take the free ones), palettes.json merged row by row. kind song takes a base64 .mid, which becomes song.json (importMidi) and is what music(0) plays. Returns the importer's stats, the toy's VRAM budget and any warnings; the panels' own readers must accept the merged files or the toy is left alone. Clears the run.

png.description: a base64 PNG (8-bit grey, RGB, RGBA or palette)

mid.description: for kind song: a Standard MIDI File, base64

grid.description: the hand-drawn form: pixels are palette indices, -1 is transparent

palette.description: the grid's palette: a list of [r, g, b] (0..255)

kind.description: what the source becomes; song takes mid

size.description: the pattern size for kind sprites (16x16, 32x16, 16x32, 32x32, 16x64 or 32x64)

maxPalettes.description: cap the palette rows the importer may use

name: song_write
description: Compose the toy's song (#161) with the SEQUENCER's built-in instruments and write it as song.json, the file music(index) plays and the studio's SEQUENCER edits. Two forms: notes (a step list [{channel, step, note, length, instrument}], note a name like "C4" or the engine note 0..83, instrument a built-in name or index) over a grid of `steps` columns; or song, the SEQUENCER's own document. The song is compiled by renderer/pce-seq.js before anything changes, so a refused song leaves the toy alone. Clears the run.

notes.description: the step list: one object per note

note.description: a note name (C4) or the engine note 0..83

instrument.description: a built-in name (lead, bass, bell, strings, kick, snare) or an index

song.description: the SEQUENCER's document: {name, tempo, swing, key, steps, patterns, order, instruments} (pce-seq.js VERSION)

name: frame_png
description: Render one frame of the current run as a PNG (256x224 RGB) through renderer/pce-sprites.js, the one model. The frame is deterministic: asking for a frame past the run runs the missing frames first. register_set overrides are applied to the picture (view-only). Returns a text metadata block and an image content block.

frame.description: frame index; 0 is the first frame

name: registers_get
description: Read the VDC, VCE and PSG register catalogue with the names and ranges from the modules' own tables (#61): VDC BXR/BYR/CR are the settable toy registers and the other VDC names are read-only; VCE CR/CTA/CTW; PSG R0..R9 (renderer/pce-psg.js). Live values come from the current run and its overrides. Pass addr to read one CRAM colour word (VCE CTW).

name: register_set
description: Set one register as a reversible view override on the current run. VDC BXR/BYR/CR take the host's ranges and refuse with reg-range/reg-forbidden (renderer/pce-toyhost.js). VCE CTW writes one 9-bit colour at addr (pal-range). PSG R0..R9 records a write in the toy's sound stream (renderer/pce-psg.js's widths). value:null clears a VDC or VCE override and restores the toy's own value.

name.description: BXR, BYR, CR, CTW or R0..R9

value.description: the register value; null clears an override

addr.description: the CRAM address for VCE CTW

name: validate
description: Run #32's validator (renderer/pce-validate.js) on the loaded toy and return its findings with file:line, the cycle budget, sprites per line, VRAM, ROM estimate and the raster blank. ok:false carries the first refusal's code (validate-frame-budget, validate-sprite-line, validate-rom, validate-range, reg-range, ...).

frames.description: frames the validator runs the toy for

name: export_pce
description: Export the loaded toy to a .pce through #100's browser route (no compiler): IL -> pce-ilbc bytecode -> pce-rom.buildToyRom over the committed renderer/ilvm.bin. The validator runs first and a toy it fails is refused by code. Default output is $TMPDIR/pce-mcp/<name>.pce; pass out for another path. The llvm-mos route (tools/toyc) exists where llvm-mos is installed but is not called here.

name: docs
description: Read #61's toy author's reference, generated from the modules' own tables. No topic lists the chapters; a topic id (the-toy, registers, palettes, sprites, raster, pads, timer, passwords, sound, budgets, refusals) returns that chapter as markdown. Use it before guessing a call name or limit.

topic.description: a chapter id or title; omit for the chapter list
